findings.title: Update-flow all-timed-out test bypasses loader
findings.problem: The spec Verification requires an update-flow test where an existing index gets only timing-out new files. TestUpdateWhereEveryNewFileTimesOut raises a pre-built AllFilesTimedOutError from a mocked step, so the path loader -> AllFilesTimedOutError -> update processor error handling is never exercised end to end.
findings.impact: A regression in the loader's all-timed-out detection or in the update processor's handling of a loader-raised error would not be caught; the AC6 behaviour for updates is asserted only against an injected exception.
findings.recommendation: Drive the real FilesDatasourceLoader._load_docs_parallel with maybe_pool_submit patched to raise FileParsingTimeoutError for every file in the update flow with an existing index, and assert set_error gets the timeout message, the old index is kept and _on_process_end runs.
findings.check_notes: Test at test_file_datasource_update_processor.py:515-549 builds a real FilesDatasourceLoader, patches maybe_pool_submit to raise FileParsingTimeoutError, drains lazy_load via _process; file_loader.py:151-152 raises AllFilesTimedOutError; asserts set_error message, indices.delete not called, _on_process_end once, failed_documents == 2.

fix.change: Update-flow all-timed-out test now drives the real FilesDatasourceLoader (maybe_pool_submit patched to raise FileParsingTimeoutError for every file) through process(); asserts set_error message, old index kept, _on_process_end and failed_documents == 2

findings.title: PDF timeout test stops short of tool boundary
findings.problem: The spec Verification requires an AC8 test at each tool boundary, including the PDF tool. The added test calls PdfProcessor.extract_text_as_markdown directly with maybe_pool_submit patched, not the PDF tool's execute path. Reachability read: processor.py:237 has no wrapping except, so the production path is believed correct.
findings.impact: If a handler is later added between the tool and the processor, a pool timeout would be relabelled as a generic read error with no test failing; the stated spec verification for PDF is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that runs the PDF tool's execute path with maybe_pool_submit patched to raise FileParsingTimeoutError and asserts the timeout error surfaces (ToolException or FileParsingTimeoutError with the fixed message), not a generic read error.

disposition.rationale: processor.py:237 has no wrapping except, so the production path propagates the timeout; the processor-level test is enough
